question:
In the given figure, AB = DB and AC = DC. If ∠ABD = 58° and ∠DBC = (2x - 4)°, ∠ACB = (y + 15)° and ∠DCB = 63°, then the value of 2x + 5y is :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe9b12b09547a8fa77c5ef554e2fc92e023d282d749b39d8e16b91e112252172.png]
solution:
**Given:**

AB = DB and AC = DC.

∠ABD = 58° and ∠DBC = (2x - 4)°, 

∠ACB = (y + 15)° and ∠DCB = 63°

**Concept used:**

If all three sides of one triangle are equivalent to the corresponding three sides of the second triangle, then the two triangles are said to be congruent by SSS (Side - Side - Side) rule.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5228d31ade369e2988894918667ca647cc9f6fcbd255862f35554b06762b4aba.png] 

As AB = DB, AC = DC, and BC is common for two triangle 

So, ΔABC ≅ ΔDBC

So, ∠ABC = ∠DBC = ∠ABD/2

⇒ 58°/2 = 29°

So,

(2x - 4)° = 29°

⇒ 2x = 33°

Again,

∠ACB = ∠DCB = 63°

So,

(y + 15)° = 63°

⇒ y = 48°

So,

2x + 5y = 33° + 5 × 48°

⇒ 33° + 240°

⇒ 273°

**∴ The required answer is 273°.**
